name: Synchronous generator with brushless exciter
summary: A synchronous alternator shown with its exciter machine and rotating rectifier, as used on most generating sets.
description: Most modern generating sets use a brushless excitation system: a small exciter generator on the same shaft feeds a rotating diode rectifier, which supplies DC to the main field without slip rings. The automatic voltage regulator controls the exciter field, and some sets add a permanent-magnet pilot exciter to power the regulator independently of the output voltage.

Schematics draw the main generator circle, a smaller exciter circle on the same shaft line and a rectifier bridge between them, with the regulator connected to the exciter field. Single-line diagrams often reduce this to the main machine with a note, so the expanded form usually appears on the generator control schematic.

The symbol does not give the regulator type, the excitation support during short circuits, or whether a pilot exciter is fitted. Those determine whether the set can sustain fault current long enough for downstream protection to operate.
readingNotes: The rotating rectifier is shown inside the shaft boundary; it is not an external rectifier.
A permanent-magnet pilot exciter indicates excitation support independent of terminal voltage.
drawingChecklist: Identify regulator type and sensing connections.
distinction: This form shows the excitation chain explicitly; the plain synchronous generator symbol shows only the main machine.
